title: Board Policy 2022-07 on automated pharmacy systems: definition, prior approval request and pickup conditions
rule_summary: Board of Registration in Pharmacy Policy 2022-07, Automated Pharmacy Systems (adopted 9/1/22; revised 1/12/23), defines an Automated Pharmacy System (APS) as an automated patient-facing device that performs operations or activities, other than compounding or administration, relative to the storage, packaging, counting, labeling, and dispensing of medications, that releases patient medications after correct patient identifiers are provided, and that must have a method to collect and provide all transaction information. It states that, if approved by the Board, an APS meeting all the policy's requirements is considered an extension of the pharmacy's licensed area whether its location is contiguous or non-contiguous to the pharmacy, and that in the case of a licensed healthcare facility approval for use and placement must be obtained from the facility's licensing body. Among its conditions for dispensing Schedule IV through VI controlled substances from an APS: the APS is located within the same building as the pharmacy with the same physical address; if filled prescriptions for Schedule IV, V or Schedule VI additional drugs (i.e., gabapentin) will be stored in the APS for patient pickup, the identity of the person to whom the medication is released must be collected and maintained, all Prescription Monitoring Program reporting requirements must be met, and the DEA must be consulted for any additional requirements; in the case of new or changed therapy for the patient, the pharmacy must provide the offer to counsel; and prior to use, Board-licensed pharmacies must submit a written request for approval with details including the type of APS, the hours it will be available, the schedules of controlled substances (limited to Schedule IV through VI), security measures, and a completed Application for Pharmacy Modifications Including Remodeling, Change in Configuration, or Change in Square Footage. The policy predates 247 CMR 9.10 as published on 12/6/2024; where the two state a condition differently, such as the hours during which a pharmacist consultation is available, the regulation's text controls.
exam_relevance: Tests what the dated Board policy adds to 247 CMR 9.10: the device definition, the written request for Board approval before use, treatment of an approved APS as an extension of the licensed area, the offer to counsel for new or changed therapy, and identity and PMP handling for Schedule IV, V and gabapentin pickups.

Relying on the policy's consultation wording where 247 CMR 9.10(1)(g) requires consultation to be available during all hours the APS dispenses.
